levels.title: Warm up with a Pop CTE
levels.task: At Stellar Sound, build a CTE named pop_songs with every column from top_songs where genre = 'Pop'. Your last line must be SELECT * FROM pop_songs ORDER BY weeks_on_chart DESC, track_name. (Only that last SELECT is checked; columns follow the chart table.)
levels.initialCode: -- WITH pop_songs AS (...) SELECT * FROM pop_songs ORDER BY ...
levels.hintMessage: WITH pop_songs AS ( ... ) then SELECT from pop_songs. Think of the CTE as a short saved step.
levels.successMessage: Nice! The team can read the Pop step before the final sort.

levels.title: CTE counts, then join venues
levels.task: Stellar Sound is counting festival sets per venue. CTE perf_counts: SELECT venue_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM festival_performances GROUP BY venue_id. Join to venues. Show venue name then cnt in that order. ORDER BY cnt high to low, then name A–Z.
levels.initialCode: -- WITH perf_counts AS (SELECT venue_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt ... GROUP BY venue_id)
levels.solution:
WITH perf_counts AS (
  SELECT venue_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM festival_performances
  GROUP BY venue_id
)
SELECT v.name, p.cnt
FROM perf_counts p
JOIN venues v ON p.venue_id = v.id
ORDER BY p.cnt DESC, v.name;
levels.hintMessage: Count inside the CTE, then JOIN venues ON venue_id = id.
levels.successMessage: Perfect! Count first, then add the venue names.

levels.title: Two CTEs: chart artists who also play live
levels.task: Stellar Sound wants names that appear on the chart and on the festival stage. CTE song_artists: DISTINCT artist from top_songs. CTE perf_artists: DISTINCT artist_name from festival_performances. Join where names match. Final answer: one column artist, sorted A–Z.
levels.initialCode: -- WITH song_artists AS (...), perf_artists AS (...) SELECT ... JOIN ...
levels.hintMessage: Join ON s.artist = p.artist_name. SELECT only s.artist. ORDER BY s.artist.
levels.successMessage: Great! You matched chart names with live show names.

levels.title: CTE: only big rooms
levels.task: The tour office at Stellar Sound wants venues over 3000 seats. WITH big_venues AS (SELECT * FROM venues WHERE capacity > 3000) then SELECT * FROM big_venues ORDER BY capacity DESC, name A–Z.
levels.initialCode: -- WITH big_venues AS (SELECT * FROM venues WHERE ...) SELECT * FROM big_venues ...
levels.hintMessage: Filter inside the CTE, then select from it with a clear ORDER BY.
levels.successMessage: Good! The CTE hides the filter so the last line stays short.

levels.title: CTE: small chart snapshot
levels.task: Stellar Sound needs just two columns for a slide. CTE chart_snapshot AS (SELECT track_name, weeks_on_chart FROM top_songs). Then SELECT * FROM chart_snapshot ORDER BY weeks_on_chart DESC, track_name A–Z.
levels.initialCode: -- WITH chart_snapshot AS (SELECT track_name, weeks_on_chart FROM top_songs)
levels.hintMessage: Put ORDER BY in the last SELECT so the order always matches the answer checker.
levels.successMessage: Nice! You can reuse this small snapshot in longer homework later.
